statement: Leo has plenty of 1-cent, 2-cent, 5-cent and 10-cent coins. He wants to pay exactly 27 cents using as few coins as possible. How many coins does he use?

choices.misconception: I made 25 cents with 10 + 10 + 5 and forgot the last 2 cents.
I used two 1-cent coins at the end instead of one 2-cent coin.
I started with 5-cent coins: five of them make 25, then one 2-cent coin.
I counted the cents instead of the coins.

hints: Start with the biggest coin you can.
To use few coins, use big coins first. Take as many 10-cent coins as fit, then 5-cent coins, then 2-cent coins, then 1-cent coins.
Two 10-cent coins make 20. Then 7 cents are left. One 5-cent coin leaves 2 cents.

solutions.reliable: Use the biggest coins first. Two 10-cent coins make 20 cents, leaving 7. One 5-cent coin leaves 2. One 2-cent coin finishes it. So $10 + 10 + 5 + 2 = 27$ uses 4 coins. Three coins are not enough, since the three biggest coins give only $10 + 10 + 10 = 30$, and no three coins from the list make exactly 27. The idea to keep: for fewest coins, take the biggest coin that still fits, again and again.

whyOnTest: Paying with the fewest coins rewards working from the biggest coin down, and checking that fewer is impossible.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
